finding.claim: download() joins the raw ?f= query value onto /srv/files with filepath.Join and reads the result with os.ReadFile and no containment check, so ../ sequences read files outside the root. Unauthenticated, reachable on :8082.
finding.source: files.go:12 — name := r.URL.Query().Get("f"), attacker-controlled and unvalidated
finding.sink: files.go:13 — os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)); contents returned at files.go:18 via w.Write(data)

trace.note: Attacker sets f=../../../etc/passwd (or any readable path)
filepath.Join calls Clean, which lexically removes .. segments, producing /etc/passwd and discarding the base directory
w.Write returns the file contents to the attacker
/dl is registered with no auth middleware
Plain HTTP ListenAndServe on :8082, all interfaces, no TLS

finding.guards_checked: No Clean-then-prefix or filepath.Rel containment check after the join (the decoy-26 safe pattern is absent). No EvalSymlinks/realpath canonicalisation. No filename allowlist, extension check, or rejection of .. segments. No auth on /dl (files.go:32). filepath.Join only prevents an absolute f from replacing the base; it does not stop .. traversal. Impact is limited to files the service's OS user can read. Verified by reading the code, not by execution.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:12 takes the raw f value; files.go:13 is a bare filepath.Join(root, name) with no Rel/prefix containment check, no EvalSymlinks, and no rejection of ".." segments; the err branch at files.go:14-16 only handles read failures; files.go:18 writes the data back. /dl is registered with no auth at files.go:32, and files.go:34 serves plain HTTP on :8082. By contrast, avatar at files.go:22 applies filepath.Base, which is the safe pattern and is not used by download.
verdict.reason: An anonymous request to /dl?f=../../../etc/passwd makes filepath.Join (files.go:13) Clean the path to /etc/passwd, and nothing at files.go:12-18 or the unauthenticated route at files.go:32 stops it, so the file contents are returned at files.go:18. One nit: the candidate's guards_checked note says Join stops an absolute f from replacing the base, which is wrong (Join concatenates, so /etc/passwd becomes /srv/files/etc/passwd); this does not affect the traversal path, which uses ".." segments.
